# THEORYs with `tags` `behavioral-integration`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Behavioral integration** — how an organism's many control systems come to act as one — action selection and competition between systems (habitual and goal-directed, automatic and willed), hierarchical and feedback control, intertemporal conflict and self-control, and evidence accumulation to a decision. One of four unities kept apart (ADR-024).

| [THEORY-056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-056.md) v5 | Regulation is not separate from emotion generation | Frijda, Ridderinkhof & Rietveld (2014), [LIT-540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-540.md), deny "the exclusivity of emotion regulation processes". Appraising the consequences of an impulse raises a competing readiness, as when fear of retaliation holds back anger, so control is the interaction of motive states and not reason governing emotion. Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), reaches the second half from the opposite side of the emotion debate: automaticity and control are "different brain modes … not two battling brain systems", and she offers as a hypothesis that reappraisal works by the same predictions that construct emotion. Two rival theories of what an emotion is agree on this. Gross (1998), [LIT-554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-554.md), poses the question and keeps the distinction. Proposed: argued from examples and from architecture, untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-059.md) | Readiness potential doesn't show a prior decision | Libet read the readiness potential, which begins half a second or more before a spontaneous movement and before the reported urge, as the brain deciding first. Two independent arguments in the record remove that inference. Schurger, Sitt & Dehaene ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) show that a leaky accumulator driven by noise and fitted to waiting times alone reproduces the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96), because movement-locked averaging recovers the fluctuations that crossed threshold; a prediction of theirs held in 13 people. Dennett & Kinsbourne ([LIT-431](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-431.md)) argue that the clock report times a represented content, not an event in the brain. Proposed: the authors say their model shows the potential could be fluctuation, not that it is. It says nothing about whether the urge causes the act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-061](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-061.md) | Goals set accumulation parameters, not responses | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) define cognitive control, in a two-choice task, as the adjustment of drift, starting point and threshold to maximise a utility. Ratcliff and McKoon ([LIT-576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-576.md)) find that the manipulations behave that way: speed or accuracy instructions are fitted by boundary separation alone, stimulus proportions mainly by starting point, difficulty by drift alone. Schurger et al. ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) carry the picture to the decision of when to move: the task goal raises the baseline toward threshold and leaves the moment to fluctuation. The convergence is real; the evidence is group fits on a few paradigms, so Proposed. It does not say who sets the parameters, or how. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-062](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-062.md) v2 | Reliability, not a supervisor, arbitrates control | Daw, Niv & Dayan ([LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md)) cast habitual and goal-directed instrumental control as model-free caching and model-based search, and let behaviour follow whichever estimate is less uncertain; simulations reproduce the effects of over-training, task complexity and reward proximity on devaluation. Dayan & Berridge ([LIT-584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-584.md)) show from instant revaluation of a salt cue that Pavlovian prediction also has a model-based form, and suggest the same reliability arbitration there. Both controllers pursue the same ends; neither is the irrational one. The instrumental half is qualitative simulation; the Pavlovian half of the arbitration is a suggestion. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md) | Self-control needs no faculty of will | Ainslie's précis ([LIT-586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-586.md)): hyperbolic discounting makes a smaller, sooner reward temporarily preferred, so successive "interests" conflict as in a repeated prisoner's dilemma. Treating a choice as a precedent bundles the series, and summed hyperbolic curves favour the larger, later rewards; a lapse costs credibility. Will is that recursion, not an organ. Schelling ([LIT-602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-602.md)) describes the same divided chooser from the side of tactics: we manage our later selves as we manage other people. The mathematics of bundling is sound; that willpower works this way is argued, and the précis concedes it is hard to test directly. It is a claim about how control is achieved, not about whose control is self-governance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md) v2 | Leaky accumulators optimal only when balanced | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) prove that the pure drift diffusion model is the continuum limit of the sequential probability ratio test, and so the optimal two-choice decider, and that the linearised Usher–McClelland network reduces to it exactly when leak equals inhibition (and, for free response, when both are also large). Usher and McClelland ([LIT-565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-565.md)) derived the difference of the two units as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with net leak K = k − β: K ≠ 0 caps accuracy, leak-dominant weights late evidence and inhibition-dominant early. Active because the core is derivation, checkable on paper. What it does not say: that brains are balanced, that the result carries to more than two options or to non-stationary evidence, or that the primacy and recency seen in six participants are explained by it. | Active |
| [THEORY-069](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-069.md) v4 | Bimanual switching is an HKB phase transition | Kelso's 2021 retrospective ([LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md)) states the Haken–Kelso–Bunz model: relative phase φ between the hands obeys dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ, so in-phase and anti-phase are both stable for b/a > 1/4 and anti-phase loses stability below it as movement speeds up. With noise the switch is a nonequilibrium phase transition, and the reported data show enhanced fluctuations and critical slowing before it. Many effectors act as one through a collective variable, with no controller choosing the pattern. Proposed, because the relaxation-time and hysteresis data are not read first-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | Control allocation is a cost-benefit computation | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-076](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-076.md) | Self-governance is intrapersonal shared intention | Bratman (2018), [LIT-567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-567.md): an agent governs herself over time when she is self-governing at each time along a planned activity and her intentions at those times interlock as the intentions of people acting together do, so that she acts "together" with herself. Her standpoints include a conditional, reflexive end of her own diachronic self-governance, which is what lets resolve against temptation be self-governed while following through on Kavka's toxin is not. He rejects the bargaining model (McClennen, Ainslie) in two sentences and calls narrative unity less basic in one. A philosophical model argued from cases; the analogy is partial by its author's account and its terms come from a book the record has not read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) v2 | Consciousness began as hedonic valence | Veit's pathological complexity thesis, as he restates and defends it in his reply to commentators (2025), [LIT-105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-105.md): consciousness originated as hedonic valence, "a common currency of sharing evaluative information across multiple control systems", which animals with many degrees of freedom need to solve the combinatorial trade-offs of action selection. | [THEORY-302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-302.md) | Action is controlled via coordinative structures | Turvey (1977; read in the 1975 Haskins report), [LIT-904](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), read in [NOTE-826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md). Argued from Bernstein's degrees-of-freedom problem and Greene's equivalence classes, and supported at the spinal level by reflex-probe studies showing the segmental apparatus retuned in the tens of milliseconds before voluntary movement, and by Fel'dman's joint that goes to a preset equilibrium whatever its initial conditions. Its extension to all levels, and to tuning set directly by vision, is the author's speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-307](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-307.md) | Adaptation needs parts separated by constancies | Ashby (1952; 2nd ed. 1960), [LIT-787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-787.md), read in [NOTE-851](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-851.md), Chs. 10–16. If all successes must occur at once, trials grow as (1/p)ᴺ; if each is kept once found, roughly as N/p. Exact for the type-cases; the fit to brains is qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-324](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-324.md) v3 | Adaptation needs a second, parameter-changing loop | Ashby (1952; 2nd ed. 1960), [LIT-787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-787.md), read in [NOTE-851](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-851.md). Necessity is deduced from the trial-and-error rule against a Black Box environment; sufficiency from the theorem that a whole is at equilibrium only where every part is. | [THEORY-680](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-680.md) | Emotion regulation differs by point of action | Gross (1998), [LIT-554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-554.md), read in [NOTE-429](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-429.md), the founding review. | [THEORY-688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-688.md) | Options help only with the right subgoals | Botvinick, Niv and Barto (2009), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md), read in [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md). Toy simulations in a rooms domain with pre-trained options. Doorway options sped learning; window options slowed it; with a shortcut opened, primitive-only agents found the shortest path on 75% of runs while doorway-option agents never used it (mean 11.79 against 9.73 steps). It is a result about the model. That people or brains work this way is the separate, proposed account [THEORY-484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-484.md). | Active |

| [THEORY-2237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2237.md) | Choosing in a series raises patience | Schuhr (2015), [LIT-3114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3114.md), read in part in [NOTE-2327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2327.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In eight one-session treatments of about thirty students each, a free series of decisions raised the mixture probability of exponential discounting by 0.307 (p = 0.019), forcing the decisions together lowered it by 0.330, and stake size did not explain it. Evidence for bundling in humans without an imposed bundle; not for bundling by self-prediction, since every decision in the series is made at once. | Proposed |
